Why Lila, why this role, and why at this moment in your life?
checks.expected: Lila stands out to me because this role is not just modeling in isolation; it asks for molecules to be designed on active biologics programs and for lessons from each campaign to become reusable capabilities. That matches how I have been working: building applied ML systems on biological data, testing whether representations and fusion methods actually generalize, and making research code usable for domain scientists. In my current Arborphy AI work, I built BioCLIP/EfficientNet fusion models, controlled held-out evaluations, retrieval benchmarks, and a multi-agent reasoning prototype with per-step information-gain evaluation. At this moment, after completing my M.S. in Statistics at Columbia and doing applied research across plant identification, neural imaging, and robotics, I’m ready to focus that evaluation-heavy, systems-building approach on therapeutic protein design workflows that connect ML decisions to wet-lab priorities.
